title: Scope, lifetime, storage duration and linkage
learningObjectives: Distinguish identifier scope from object storage duration.
Identify block, file and function prototype scopes.
Explain automatic, static and allocated storage durations.
Explain external and internal linkage at file scope.
Avoid using objects outside their lifetime and identifiers outside their scope.

understand.concept: Scope describes where an identifier can be used in source code. Storage duration describes the lifetime of an object's storage. Linkage describes whether declarations in different scopes or translation units refer to the same entity. These are separate properties and must not be treated as synonyms.
understand.whyItMatters: Confusing scope with lifetime or linkage causes bugs in global state, local objects, static variables and multi-file programs.
understand.analogy: Treat a function or pointer operation as an explicit contract between caller and callee.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal rules for types, object lifetime, scope and linkage.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Scope

Block scope begins at a declaration within a block and ends at the end of that block. File scope applies to declarations outside functions. Function prototype scope applies to parameter names in a prototype.

## 2. Storage duration

Automatic objects generally exist during execution of their block. Static-storage-duration objects exist for the entire program execution. Allocated storage exists from successful allocation until it is released.

## 3. Static local objects

A block-scope object declared static retains its value between function calls. Its identifier still has block scope, even though its storage duration is static.

## 4. Linkage

External linkage can make the same function or object identifiable across translation units. Internal linkage, commonly specified with static at file scope, restricts the entity to the translation unit. Some identifiers have no linkage.

## 5. Avoid lifetime errors

A pointer does not extend an object's lifetime. Do not return or retain pointers to automatic objects after their blocks end. Release allocated storage when its owner is finished.

questions.prompt: What does a static local variable retain between calls?
options: Its block scope becomes file scope
questions.explanation: Static storage duration lasts for the entire program execution.

questions.prompt: What does static at file scope commonly specify for a function or object?
questions.explanation: File-scope static gives the identifier internal linkage.

questions.prompt: Does taking an object's address extend its lifetime?
questions.explanation: A pointer does not change the object's lifetime rules.
